# Evaluation on our local test set (Phase 2)

## Purpose

CLAUDE.md section 3, Phase 2: measure the candidate models on photos of local cars that we took ourselves, sliced by
day / night / wet and by brand, and pick the best model per job with calibrated per-class confidence thresholds.
Required metrics: mask mAP50 per model, part-level recall (was each damaged part flagged?), false positives per car
(reflections, dirt), VIN OCR exact-match rate, latency, baseline vs calibrated thresholds, and a failure-case gallery
(`docs/assets/failure_cases/`). The numbers below are the deck numbers; nothing else in the deck may claim quality.

## Data status

**No labelled test set yet.** Until the `summary` block below is generated, there is no evaluation result.
`python scripts/eval.py --check` prints which inputs are present and which are missing, and `scripts/eval.py`
refuses to write any metric (exit 3) while `data/local_testset/annotations.json` is missing or has no labelled image.

Pipeline for the data (details in [labelling_guide.md](labelling_guide.md)):

1. Photos go to `data/raw/testset/{day,night,wet}/` (gitignored). VIN photos go to `data/raw/testset/vin/` and the
   true VINs to `data/raw/testset/vin_ground_truth.csv` (gitignored, never committed).
2. `scripts/blur_testset.py` blurs plates and faces (fail closed) into `data/local_testset/images/<slice>/` and
   writes `data/local_testset/slices.csv` (file, slice, brand, car, no_damage, notes).
3. Only the blurred images are uploaded to CVAT / Roboflow; damage polygons with a `part` attribute are exported as
   COCO 1.0 to `data/local_testset/annotations.json`.
4. `scripts/eval.py --split kfold:5` (or `notebooks/05_eval_local_testset.ipynb`) fills the blocks below.

## Method

**Models.** The damage models `damage_mitbersh`, `damage_danishali`, `damage_harpreet` and the parts model
`parts_mitbersh`, loaded through `avtopassport.pipeline.segment.load_segmenter` with the same image sizes as the
smoke test, on the blurred test-set images (long side 1600 px). For AP and calibration, predictions are kept down to
score 0.01 (ultralytics' own validation uses 0.001; 0.01 bounds the runtime and can only lower AP slightly).

**Ground truth.** COCO polygons only (RLE and `iscrowd` are rejected). Polygons are rasterised in numpy with the
pixel-centre rule (a pixel belongs to the polygon when its centre is inside, even-odd rule); several polygons of one
annotation are merged. Damage class names are compared case-insensitively with `_` / `-` treated as spaces
(`Glass_Shatter` = `glass shatter`). A GT class that a model does not predict is listed as "not in model vocabulary"
and excluded from that model's mean AP (its instances still count for part recall).

**Mask AP50.** Per class: predictions of all images sorted by score; each prediction is matched to the unmatched GT
instance of the same class on the same image with the highest mask IoU, if that IoU is >= 0.5 (greedy, COCO style);
otherwise it is a false positive. AP is the 101-point interpolated area under the precision envelope (as in COCO).
mAP50 is the mean over the classes that have GT in the slice. The predicted masks come from the model's polygons
(`retina_masks=False`, rasterised with OpenCV), the GT masks from the numpy rasteriser; boundary pixels can differ by
about one pixel, which matters only for very thin damage (scratches).

**Part-level recall.** Unit: a (image, part) pair that has at least one GT damage polygon with that `part` attribute.
It counts as found if any kept prediction of any damage class either (a) is assigned to that part by
`mapping.assign` with the parts model's masks (largest overlap, `MIN_OVERLAP` 0.2), or (b) has mask IoU >= 0.1 with a
GT polygon of that part. Rule (b) catches correct detections whose part assignment failed; the tables show how many
parts were found by rule (a). The damage class does not have to be right: the question is "was the part flagged".

**False positives.** Per clean car: all kept predictions on images tagged `no_damage`, divided by the number of
distinct cars (`car` column of `slices.csv`; one image = one car when it is empty). Per image: kept predictions that
match no GT (IoU 0.5, same class), over all evaluated images.

**Thresholds and calibration.** Baseline: conf 0.25 for every class (ultralytics' default, what the pipeline runs
today). Calibrated: per class, the score threshold that maximises F1 at IoU 0.5 (keep predictions with score >=
threshold; equal scores are kept or dropped together; F1 ties go to the higher threshold; a class with no GT or no
true positive keeps 0.25). Calibrating and reporting on the same images is optimistic, so `--split kfold:K`
(or `holdout:F`) splits by car, calibrates on the other folds and reports the held-out result; the summary uses the
held-out numbers when a split is given and says "IN-SAMPLE" otherwise.

**Slices.** `all`, `day`, `night`, `wet` (from the input folder / `slices.csv`), and `brand:<X>` for every brand
filled in `slices.csv`. Small slices give unstable numbers; the image and GT counts are printed next to every metric.

**VIN.** For each row of `data/raw/testset/vin_ground_truth.csv` (`file,vin`), `vin.ocr.read_vin` on
`data/raw/testset/vin/<file>`. Exact match = status `read` and all 17 characters equal; `ambiguous` counts as a
miss. Only counts and rates are written.

**Latency.** Median and p90 of `segment()` per image (prediction + mask rasterisation) on the device of the run,
after one warm-up image, at conf 0.25, on up to 20 test images. Full-inspection latency on the deploy CPU is a
Phase 4 measurement.

**Failure cases.** Per model, up to 12 images with the most errors (missed GT + false positives) at the calibrated
thresholds, drawn on the blurred images: red = missed GT, yellow = false positive, green = true positive.

## Model choice

To be written from the generated tables once they exist (which damage model, which thresholds), with a short ADR in
`docs/decisions/`.

## Limitations

- The test set is small (60-100 cars at most), collected in Tashkent parking lots by the team; per-slice numbers on a
  few dozen cars have wide confidence intervals and must be quoted with their counts.
- Labels come from the team, not from body-shop experts; a single labeller per image, no agreement study.
- Images are blurred before labelling and evaluation; a damage under a blurred plate region is invisible to the model
  and to the labeller.
- Calibrated thresholds are tuned on this set. Only held-out (`--split`) numbers estimate how they generalise.
- Mask AP on thin damage (scratches) is sensitive to polygon precision; part-level recall is the more robust
  product metric.
- Latency is measured on the machine that ran the evaluation, not on the deploy host.
- Licences: the damage checkpoints were trained on CarDD (non-commercial research use); see
  `docs/research/model_candidates.md`.
